title: Effects of Serum 25-Hydroxyvitamin D Level on Bone Mineral Density in Type 2 Diabetes
author: Liting Guo
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.kjycupw

steps.title: Obtain ethics approval and consent
steps.instruction: Secure approval from the Independent Ethics Committee of Teda International Cardiovascular Hospital and obtain written informed consent from all participants before any study procedures.

steps.title: Recruit study participants
steps.instruction: Randomly select 368 patients with type 2 diabetes (165 males, 203 females, ages 40–79) from the endocrinology departments of General Hospital, Tianjin Medical University and Teda International Cardiovascular Hospital (January 2014–June 2016) and 300 non‑diabetic control subjects matched for age, body‑mass index, smoking and alcohol history from the same hospitals.

steps.title: Apply inclusion criteria
steps.instruction: Include diabetic subjects who meet the 1999 WHO diagnostic criteria for type 2 diabetes; include control subjects who have normal blood glucose, lipid profile, and blood pressure.

steps.title: Apply exclusion criteria
steps.instruction: Exclude any subject with hyperthyroidism, hyperparathyroidism, Paget’s disease, severe hepatopathy, nephropathy, neoplastic disease, or who is pregnant or lactating; also exclude anyone taking corticosteroids, gonadal hormones, immunosuppressants, anticonvulsants, thiazolidinediones (diabetes group only), or any drugs affecting bone metabolism (vitamin D or derivatives, calcium, diphosphonates) within the past six months.

steps.title: Measure bone mineral density
steps.instruction: Using a LUNAR dual‑energy X‑ray absorptiometry (DEXA) scanner, have the same operator measure BMD (g/cm²) at lumbar spine (L1–L4), femoral neck, total hip, and total body for each participant; calculate the lumbar spine value as the mean of L1–L4, compute T‑scores based on age‑ and gender‑matched Chinese reference values, and classify osteoporosis when BMD ≤ ‑1.0 SD.

steps.title: Group diabetic participants
steps.instruction: Divide the diabetic cohort into four sub‑groups based on diabetes duration (≤10 years vs >10 years) and HbA1c level (≤8 % vs >8 %).

steps.title: Perform biochemical measurements
steps.instruction: Collect and analyze blood samples for relevant biochemical parameters (e.g., HbA1c) as described in the study protocol.
